A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KSTER attack and subspace camouflage defense. All 33 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original attack and defense experiments across three language models, CounterFact and zsRE, alongside utility evaluations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds end-to-end extraction, sequential editing, candidate-pool sensitivity, baseline comparisons and decoy-factuality results.

M1.justification: The spectral subject-inference procedure, relative-entropy prompt scoring and camouflage update remain unchanged. Algorithm 1's explicit initialization and Algorithm 3's added listing of P clarify existing operations. Querying the original model for recovered outputs was already described in v1.

E1.justification: The original benchmarks remain, but v2 adds evaluation of original-output extraction, cumulative sequential edits and factual knowledge about decoy subjects (Tables 3, 13 and 17). Candidate-pool experiments also introduce IMDb names and generated prompt templates, extending the represented candidate populations beyond the original libraries.

E2.justification: V2 adds a post-edit-only minimum-entropy baseline for prompt recovery, defined in Appendix E.1 and evaluated in Table 15. Table 16 additionally evaluates camouflage against the existing gray-box subject attack; v1's defense evaluation used the white-box attacker. Original subject-inference comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include 2–10 cumulative edits with N=100 and Top-(s×N) recall, subject pools from 2,000 to 10 million, and prompt pools from 1,000 to 10,000. V2 also introduces end-to-end recall and decoy True Fact Recall using rewrite/paraphrase prompts. These supplement the retained experimental settings rather than establish reruns of the original comparisons.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds subject- and prompt-pool sensitivity studies, sequential-edit robustness, defense testing against a gray-box attacker, and analysis of decoy hallucinations. These address substantial additional questions about scalability and defense side effects. The covariance and generic-template analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results average five independent runs and retain existing uncertainty displays. However, v2's new Table 3 and Tables 12–17 report point estimates without the variability shown in v1's result tables. No increased run count or new statistical test is documented.

E6.justification: All ten original tables retain their numerical results after matching. V2 adds substantial outcomes: Table 3 reports CounterFact end-to-end Top-20 recall of 0.78, 0.74 and 0.81 for GPT-J, Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5, respectively; Tables 12–17 report the additional analyses and comparisons. The CounterFact utility plots also change the undefended reference rank from 1 to approximately 50.8 (v1 Figures 5/7; v2 Figures 4/6).

T1.justification: V2 corrects the maximum-principal-angle definition and changes the upper bound in Equation 35 from max to min. It also repairs ROME normalization and missing or incorrect K/P factors in existing derivations, distinguishes edit keys from generic-template keys, and qualifies covariance convergence through matrix-concentration conditions. The existing theorem framework is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the central claims about update leakage, two-stage reconstruction and subspace camouflage. Original-output extraction was already asserted in v1; v2 supplies direct evidence for that goal. The conclusion's wording changes do not establish a different core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's unresolved sequential-attack limitation and interprets the new cumulative-edit results positively. It adds decoy hallucination as a specific defense limitation while retaining candidate-pool dependence and concerns about long-term defense utility. Some new interpretations overreach: the claimed prompt-pool recall decline of at most 2% contradicts Table 14's larger zsRE declines.

D1.justification: V2 documents IMDb sampling, generation of 9,000 additional templates with Gemini 3.1 Pro, and the minimum-entropy baseline procedure. It clarifies pseudocode inputs and initialization and changes the advertised repository from EditingAtk.git to EditingAttack. Existing implementation settings remain largely unchanged; repository availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B add Youssef et al. (2025), distinguishing reversal of model behavior from prompt/output reconstruction. Appendix B also adds Liu et al. (2026a, 2026b) on forward replay and locality evaluation. These are limited positioning additions, not newly evaluated external baselines.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative remain intact. V2 moves limitations to Appendix A, separates implementation details from additional experiments, and gives defense theory its own appendix. It also makes localized language, cross-reference, pseudocode-documentation and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the result displays with the end-to-end table and six appendix tables covering new evaluation questions. It relocates the covariance figure from the main text to Appendix F, reorders existing tables, resizes figures and adjusts CounterFact utility-plot axes. Existing figures are retained rather than replaced by new analyses.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves an important evidential gap: v1 explicitly omitted original-output recovery, whereas Table 3 directly evaluates end-to-end extraction. Larger candidate pools, sequential edits, a simple prompt baseline and decoy-factuality tests substantially strengthen validation and expose defense costs. Mathematical corrections improve reliability. Missing variability in new tables and overstated summaries remain weaknesses—for example, Table 14 reports a zsRE decline from 0.63 to 0.52 despite the claimed 2% maximum—but the added validation and corrected reasoning provide a substantial net improvement.
